items.headline: Agencies Treating AI Efficiency as Margin, Not Discount

WPP has shifted a substantial share of net sales to performance-based terms. Hourly billing is fading fastest; productized per-deliverable packages see the widest margin expansion.
items.action: Never discount because AI made the work faster. Price on output value and let AI-driven speed flow to margin.

items.headline: Lightbringer Hits 200 Clients With Full-Stack AI Service
items.body: Swedish AI-native patent firm Lightbringer reported 200+ clients across 17 countries and 300% YoY revenue growth. The company employs both AI and patent attorneys in-house, delivering filings in days at roughly 50% the cost of traditional firms. Owning both the AI and the professional under one roof beats selling software.
items.action: Study Lightbringer's full-stack model as a template: AOM already owns the AI and creative talent.

items.headline: White-Label AI Agents Now a $1M ARR Line for Agencies
items.body: Agencies reselling white-label AI voice and chat agents are reporting $50K-$150K in new recurring revenue, with top performers hitting $1M ARR from 30-50 clients. Platforms like Synthflow and GoHighLevel offer turnkey infrastructure while agencies charge clients $500-$1,500/month at 70-80% gross margins.
items.action: Evaluate adding a branded AI receptionist or lead qualifier at $500-1K/month as a sticky add-on to creative retainers.

items.headline: DeepSeek V4 Pro Ships: 1.6T Params at $0.44/M Input
items.body: DeepSeek's flagship V4 Pro left preview on August 13. It is a mixture-of-experts model with 1.6 trillion total parameters (49B active per token), a 1M-token context window, and 384K max output. API pricing lands at $0.435/M input and $0.87/M output, making it one of the cheapest frontier-class models available.
items.action: Test DeepSeek V4 Pro as a cost-efficient worker model for high-volume agent tasks like research and lead enrichment.

items.headline: Cloudflare Agents Week: Full Infra Stack for AI Agents
items.body: Cloudflare shipped a comprehensive agent infrastructure suite: sandboxed compute environments with shell and filesystem, Git-compatible Artifacts storage, Cloudflare Mesh for private agent networking, Email Service in public beta, and Browser Run with Live View and 4x concurrency.
items.action: Evaluate Cloudflare Sandboxes and Browser Run as the runtime layer for AOM's dispatched agents.

items.headline: MCP Goes Stateless: The Biggest Protocol Shift Yet
items.body: The MCP 2026-07-28 spec dropped the bidirectional stateful protocol for request/response where every request is self-describing and independent. Servers can now deploy on serverless and edge infrastructure. The spec also brings OAuth 2.0/OIDC authorization hardening and a formal extensions framework for MCP Apps and Tasks.
items.action: Audit AOM's MCP server configs for compatibility with the stateless spec.

items.headline: Seedance 2.5: 30-Second AI Video With 50 References
items.body: ByteDance's Seedance 2.5 doubles clip length to 30 seconds in a single pass and accepts up to 50 multimodal references per generation. It supports region-level redraw editing, native sound, and up to 4K output. Available on Dreamina and fal.ai with no waitlist.
items.action: Run a side-by-side comparison of Seedance 2.5 vs current pipeline on an upcoming client social reel.

items.headline: Claude Code 2.1.229: Server Hooks and Plugin Marketplace
items.body: The August 12 Claude Code release adds server-supplied hook support for self-hosted runner sessions, a plugin marketplace with dynamic command sources, and SSE keepalive pings during long thinking pauses. It also fixes MCP OAuth sign-in and adds Remote Control session resume via --continue.
items.action: Update Claude Code to 2.1.231 across all AOM terminals and test the plugin marketplace.

items.headline: Devin Desktop ships Spaces + Subagents: shared-context containers for multi-agent work
items.body: Cognition's Devin Desktop added "Spaces" (July 29) that group agent sessions, PRs, files and context into one task-level container so multiple agents — Devin, Claude Agent, Codex, OpenCode — share the same working understanding via the open Agent Client Protocol. Aug 10 added a full Subagents management panel, flat agents/<name>.md subagent definitions, and org-level permission composition where an explicit deny always wins.
items.action: Prototype a Space-style container for Corner rooms bundling a task's chat, files, and worker sessions, and audit permission composition against theirs.

items.headline: MCP 2026-07-28 spec goes stateless and formalizes a Tasks lifecycle for long-running work
items.body: The Model Context Protocol's July 28 release moved from a stateful, session-based model to stateless request/response (serverless/edge-deployable) and graduated MCP Tasks to an official extension: tool calls return a task handle that clients poll via tasks/get, tasks/update, tasks/cancel. MCP Apps also graduated, letting servers render interactive UI inline in a conversation.
items.action: Map Corner's dispatched-task/worker pattern onto the MCP Tasks handle model so external tools could poll a Corner worker without a custom integration.

items.headline: Klaviyo acquires AI agent startup Agency, absorbing 25-person team into its marketing/support agents
items.body: Klaviyo announced Aug 5, 2026 it's acquiring Agency, the AI-native customer-engagement startup founded by Elias Torres ($32M raised from Sequoia, Menlo, Felicis), who becomes Klaviyo's Chief Product Officer. The deal folds Agency's proactive AI agents into Klaviyo's Composer (AI campaign builder) and Customer Agent products, using Klaviyo's claimed 9 billion consumer profiles as the data layer — a template for how big martech platforms are buying AI-agency capability outright instead of building it.
items.action: Position AOM's pitch around judgment and brand-specific creative direction that platform-bundled AI agents can't replicate.

items.headline: Meta Business Agent starts charging per-token (~$2/M tokens) from Aug 1, 2026 after 1M-business pilot
items.body: Meta's AI agent for WhatsApp/Instagram/Messenger — which fields customer inquiries, books appointments, vets leads, and completes transactions — moved from free pilot to metered paid usage on Aug 1, 2026, following a rollout that hit over 1 million businesses in pilot markets before its June global launch. Meta is now directly monetizing the AI-front-desk function small businesses previously paid agencies or dedicated tools to handle.
